A Servant can be Desynchronized when cut.message: A Servant can be Desynchronized when cut off from The Synchronous' massive distributed network architecture. Some that are describe the experience of being Synchronized as one where purpose and directive are always clearly defined--something often comforting to commanders in this dark age, but antithetical to others that seek to be something greater than themselves.
A Servant can be Desynchronized when cut.description: Lore paragraph for the Synchronous faction, one of five shown at random as the description of a Synchronous-held system in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Stock Planetary Annihilation flavour text: The Synchronous, Servant, Synchronized/Desynchronized are faction terms; keep "--" as a dash. Full paragraph, keep the final full stop. (gw_faction_2.js:139)

A map pack this war uses is missing.message: A map pack this war uses is missing

A mystery..description: Tooltip on the faction heading in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map, shown for the "Guardians" faction (the mirror-mode enemy that fields the player's own loadout), in place of a real faction description. A neural network thought to have origina.message: A neural network thought to have originally been used to train new commanders, it has continued its training cycles while they slumbered and is now the deadliest force in the galaxy.
A neural network thought to have origina.description: Lore description for the neutral-system topic "Queller" (the Queller AI). Shown in the Planetary Intelligence panel for a neutral (unowned) system when the "System Lore" game option is on, under the heading "Queller". Full paragraph; keep the final full stop. (lore.js:38)

A race this war fields is missing.message: A race this war fields is missing
A race this war fields is missing.description: Tooltip on the disabled Fight/Explore button on the galaxy map (gw_play) when the war uses a race (unit-set mod such as Legion, Bugs or Exiles) that is not installed or enabled. "Fields" = uses in battle. Short sentence, no trailing full stop in the original. (races.js:90)

ADVANCED FABBERS:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a dropdown of numbers and means the maximum number of advanced fabbers (T2 builder units) the AI may have per army; its tooltip is "Maximum number of advanced fabbers per army." Noun phrase, plural, upper-case; keep the trailing colon. The sibling label is "BASIC FABBERS:". (ai_settings.html:173)

AI.description: Title of the AI picker dialog on the war setup screen (gw_start), and the label of the button in the co-op setup strip that opens it, beside "Commander" and "Game Options". The dialog holds the Race / Opponent / ALLY / Co-op table of AI brains. Noun, singular, the initialism for artificial intelligence; no punctuation. The same word as the game's "AI:" label with the colon removed, so use that translation without the colon (KI, IA, SI, ИИ, 电脑, or AI where the game keeps the English). (ai_modal.html:6, ai_modal.html:23)

AI Commander.description: Marker after an AI player's name in the co-op lobby's slot list on the galaxy map (gw_play), read as "<name> - AI Commander", the way the host's own row reads "<name> - Host". The game's own string, from the skirmish lobby's AI slots; use the game's translation. Noun phrase, singular, no punctuation. (coop_ai_slot.html:2)

AI Settings.description: Title/header of the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Noun phrase, plural ("Settings"), title case, no punctuation. (ai_settings.html:3)

AI Tech.description: Heading (h3) on the galaxy map's system intelligence panel, above the list of tech cards the enemy AI in that system holds; a "?" tooltip beside it reads "Applied to AI commanders and units preferred by the faction." Noun phrase, title case, no punctuation. "Tech" is the game's word for a tech card; reuse the stock rendering, and keep "AI" as the game writes it. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.html:50)

AI:.description: Label in the war-info panel of the galaxy map (gw_play), used three times: after "Opponent" ("Opponent AI:"), after "ALLY" ("Ally AI:", the CSS lower-cases ALLY), and in a co-op session after "Co-op" ("Co-op AI:"), and followed by the AI brain name (Titans, Queller, Penchant). "AI" is a noun (the AI brain), singular; keep the trailing colon. The preceding words are separate strings, so the phrase is assembled by juxtaposition in that order. (gwo_panel.html:34, gwo_panel.html:45)

ALLY.description: Column header "ALLY" in the AI modal table on the war setup screen (Race / Opponent / ALLY / Co-op, the AI brain used for allied commanders), and in the war-info panel where it is displayed sentence-cased before "AI:" ("Ally AI:"). Also appended in brackets to a faction name in the Planetary Intelligence panel: "<Faction> (ALLY)" for the faction that fights on the player's side. Noun, singular. Uses the base game's existing "ALLY" entry, so match that translation. (gwo_panel.html:39, section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:86, ai_modal.html:42)

ALLY CHANCE:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "ARKYD" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "ARKYD Upgrade Tech increases the vision and radar of the basic orbital radar by 50%."; keep the two consistent. ARKYD Upgrade Tech increases the vision.message: ARKYD Upgrade Tech increases the vision and radar of the basic orbital radar by 50%.

The game appends the separate string 'Adds a new slot for another technology.' after this text, so do not add that idea here. (gwaio_upgrade_arkyd.js:8)

(gw_faction_0.js:103 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:40)

After a hundred years of warfare, the on.message: After a hundred years of warfare, the only thing on the minds of citizens of the Progenitor Coalition was a lasting peace. The General Assembly agreed, and the Myr Project was born. Contracting explorer ships from Lusk Exploration Company, the Progenitor Coalition government commissioned a search for a suitable system to turn into the ultimate destination for rest and relaxation for civilian and military alike. The result was Myr, a system where any type of leisure activity that one could think of could be experienced in the system.

After making their fortune in the Progen.message: After making their fortune in the Progenitor galactic real estate market, the Rittenhouse family of the Sancruzo system decided it was time to find a planet to call their very own. They found here, a good distance from the commerce centers of neighboring systems, but not far enough to be isolated from the ebb and flow of Coalition life. The system they settled in they simply named after the family. From majestic alpine vistas to warm tropical beaches, Rittenhouse once offered much. By the time of the Century War the Rittenhouse family employed a private security force that included several orbital weapon platforms, all to keep strangers away from the system.

After the end of the Century War, Comman.message: After the end of the Century War, Commanders were being decommissioned and needed to be integrated into the civilian workforce. The system of Varthema served as the diagnostic and retraining center for them. Before the outset of the Pro-Com War, Machine Liberation Army (MLA) leader Tryphon condemned Varthema as a 'laboratory run by mad scientists who turned a Commander into an obedient slave of the Progenitor.' When the system was captured by MLA forces late in the war, Tryphon ordered the system 'scraped clean' of any signs of biological life- with the Progenitors and all their creations at the top of the list.

After the end of the Century War, Progen.message: After the end of the Century War, Progenitor High Command (PHC) of the Progenitor Coalition came under pressure from the General Assembly to restructure the military back to peacetime numbers. The only problem was that many veteran's home worlds had been devastated during the war and their families killed. As a solution, PHC, with the approval of the General Assembly, chose the Rawat system as its primary reintegration center for all human service members transitioning from the military back to civilian life. This would later be recognized as one of a series of mistakes made by the Progenitor Coalition that would cause a rift between many of the Commanders and humans.

After their first victory over the Machi.message: After their first victory over the Machine Liberation Army (MLA) forces at Seven Gates, the Progenitor Coalition went on the offensive. Progenitor High Command selected the system Omicron Herculis and its valuable resources as its first target. With a fleet of transports carrying over a million Progenitor soldiers and escorted by a NEST, they successfully breached the system and established a base of operations. The NEST made short work of the MLA Commanders in the system, while Progenitor Marines mopped up the remaining enemy forces.

Agoge was the center for all military tr.message: Agoge was the center for all military training for the Progenitor Coalition. Progenitor soldiers before the Century War were used to training for quelling planetary riots and pirate activities, to name a few. Very few major conflicts had erupted in the Progenitor Coalition for over three hundred years. That all changed with the Xziphid Hegemony. Progenitor High Command soon discovered its troops were ill prepared to fight the type of war they were facing with the Xziphid. Training for new recruits became harsh and brutal, with many 'washing out'. Marines had it especially hard, being they would be the ones to go toe to toe with the enemy in all kinds of environments. In the end, the Progenitor Coalition had created the finest soldiers humanity had ever seen, but they still weren't enough to stop the Xziphid. It would take the advent of the Commanders to save humanity from extinction.

Aryabhata was a mineral rich system, esp.message: Aryabhata was a mineral rich system, especially known for the ultra-rare Mortolite; a gemstone used in the manufacturing of the most powerful beam weapons that were used by Progenitor Coalition military. As a result, protecting the system was paramount. At the outset of the Pro-Com War, the Machine Liberation Army (MLA) made capturing Aryabhata a priority. Seven major battles were fought over the system, with the MLA failing to capture it until the final years of the war.

As the Progenitor Coalition began to exp.message: As the Progenitor Coalition began to expand, settlers from the Sol System began a long voyage in a fleet of over twenty merchant ships they had bought to find a system they could call their own; free to practice their religion without what they perceived as ridicule and persecution. Led by the charismatic Jack Smithington, the group found their home in the Janszoon System. When Machine Liberation Army (MLA) forces reached the system during the final years of the Pro-Com War, they encountered such fierce resistance that they were forced to saturate the system with nukes. Over three billion people were systematically erased from the galaxy in only a matter of minutes.

In a last-ditch attempt to halt the MLA advance, Progenitor forces peppered the system with a barrage of nuclear warheads. The MLA advance had been stopped, but the scorched earth tactics had rendered the system a radioactive wasteland. Azaghul gambled on the system for producing large amounts of metals, and they were not disappointed. As it turned out, Fier produced a new type of iron, which Azaghul scientist labeled 'Dragon'. Banno was the home of the Great Banno Lo.message: Banno was the home of the Great Banno Lottery, held every ten years among its billions of citizens spread among the system. Every ten years, with great ceremony, a drawing would be held and broadcast throughout the Progenitor Coalition selecting one winner. The individual chosen would receive two billion Coalition credits. The only catch was that once the person died any remaining money would pass back into the lottery pool. In the years before the system fell to the Machine Liberation Army (MLA) the lottery prize pool held over one hundred and fifty billion Coalition credits.

The city effectively remained hidden from Machine Liberation Army (MLA) forces until the very end of the war when a captured Progenitor memory node revealed its location. The city, along with the sea, disappeared in mushroom clouds of radioactive fire.

Bot Armor Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card raises the health of all bots by 50%. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must match the opening words of the description 'Bot Armor Tech increases health...'. (gwc_health_bots.js:10)

Bot Armor Tech increases health of all b.message: Bot Armor Tech increases health of all bots by 50%
Bot Armor Tech increases health of all b.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: health of every bot x1.5. Keep '50%'; the source has no final full stop. Opening words must be identical to the card name 'Bot Armor Tech'. (gwc_health_bots.js:8)

Bot Combat Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card gives all bots +50% health, +25% damage and +50% speed. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must match the opening words of the description 'Bot Combat Tech increases health of all bots...'. (gwc_combat_bots.js:11)

Bot Combat Tech increases health of all.message: Bot Combat Tech increases health of all bots by 50%, damage by 25%, and speed by 50%
Bot Combat Tech increases health of all.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Combat Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies max health and movement speed of every mobile bot by 1.5 and the damage of bot weapons by 1.25. Keep 50%, 25% and 50% exactly. 'Bot' here is the unit class (bipedal walkers built at a Bot Factory), not a robot in general; use the game's own term for Bot. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Combat Tech'. There is no full stop at the end in English. (gwc_combat_bots.js:9)

Bot Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout gives the player the basic bot factory and basic bots at the start of the war. Noun phrase, a title: 'Commander' is the player's commander unit, 'Bot' is the unit class it favours. Follow the pattern used by the other '<X> Commander' loadout names so they read as one series. Must agree with the card text 'The Bot Commander loadout contains basic bot factories.' (gwc_start_bot.js:18)

Bot Cooldown Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card halves the cooldown time between builds for every bot factory (basic and advanced). Short title, noun phrase; 'Cooldown' is the factory's pause between finishing one unit and starting the next. Keep the game's own term for Tech and Bot. Must match the wording used at the start of its description 'Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown time...'. (gwaio_cooldown_bots.js:10)

Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown ti.message: Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown time between builds for all bot factories.
Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown ti.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Cooldown Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies factory_cooldown_time of every bot factory by 0.5, so a bot factory starts its next unit twice as quickly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Cooldown Tech'. (gwaio_cooldown_bots.js:8)

Bot Engine Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card increases the movement speed of all mobile bots by 50%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Engine' is figurative (it is a speed upgrade). Must match the opening words of its description 'Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all bots by 50%'. (gwc_speed_bots.js:10)

Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all b.message: Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all bots by 50%
Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all b.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Engine Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the movement, acceleration and turn rates of every mobile bot by 1.5. Keep 50% exactly; there is no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Engine Tech'. (gwc_speed_bots.js:8)

Bot Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card cuts the metal build cost of every mobile bot by 25%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Fabrication' is the game's word for construction. Must match the opening words of its description 'Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all bots by 25%'. (gwc_cost_bots.js:10)

Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build.message: Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all bots by 25%
Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Fabrication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies build_metal_cost of every mobile bot by 0.75. 'Metal' is one of the game's two resources; use its standard translation. Keep 25% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Fabrication Tech'. (gwc_cost_bots.js:8)

Bot Factory.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. This is a stock Planetary Annihilation unit; use the game's existing translation of that unit's display name so the tooltip matches the in-game build bar. Noun, singular, title case. The same English text is also registered as a race-specific unit name (race descriptor unitNames) for the Bugs/Exiles races, where the race's own unit has the same name; keep the two identical. (unit_names.js:36, exiles.js:454)

Bot Factory Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_botfactory, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Bot Factory"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the building of advanced units by basic bot manufacturing."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_botfactory.js)

Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the bui.message: Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the building of advanced units by basic bot manufacturing.
Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the bui.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Bot Factory Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'Basic bot manufacturing' means the basic Bot Factory building: after this card it can produce advanced (tier 2) bots. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Factory Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_botfactory.js:11)

Bounties.description: Game modifier name listed under "Game Modifiers" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line, and in the win-conditions line of the in-game HUD (live_game), where modifiers are joined with " | ". "Bounties" = every kill earns an economy multiplier; in the HUD it may be followed by " x<value>". Noun, plural, no punctuation; must match "BOUNTIES" in the Game Modifiers tooltip and the "Bounties Chance" label. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:241, win_conditions_text.js:27)

Bounties Chance.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a percentage dropdown; tooltip: "Chance of a system awarding bounties for army kills." Title case (CSS up-cases it on screen), no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). Noun phrase; "Bounties" must match the modifier name. Sibling: "Bounty Value". (ai_settings.html:486)

Bounty Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card switches on the Bounties game modifier (kill an enemy commander, receive a resource bounty) in every battle of the war. Short title, noun phrase. 'Bounties' is a stock game mode name; use the game's existing translation. Must agree with the description 'Bounty tech enables the bounties game modifier in every system.' (gwaio_enable_bounties.js:9)

Bounty Value.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a dropdown of multipliers; tooltip: "Eco bonus per army kill." Title case (CSS up-cases it on screen), no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). Noun phrase, singular. (ai_settings.html:509)

Bounty tech enables the bounties game mo.message: Bounty tech enables the bounties game modifier in every system.
Bounty tech enables the bounties game mo.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bounty Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card turns on the stock 'Bounties' game modifier for every star system (battle) in the war. 'Bounties' should use the game's existing translation of that game mode. 'System' means a star system on the galaxy map. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bounty Tech' (English lower-cases 'tech' here; follow your locale's rule). (gwaio_enable_bounties.js:7)

Bronze.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. (difficulty_levels.js:89)

Buff Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started, as the locked-loadout tooltip while it is still locked, and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout gives all units 30% more health and damage but 25% less speed and 30% higher cost. Noun phrase, a title. 'Buff' is slang for strong/muscular (and a gaming term for a stat boost); render the sense of 'beefed-up', not a colour. Follow the pattern of the other '<X> Commander' loadout names. (tgw_start_tank.js:42)

Bugs.description: Name of the Bugs race (an alien unit set from the Bugs faction mod). Used as the heading of the neutral-system lore topic about the Bugs in the Planetary Intelligence panel, and as the race's name in race pickers, the AI modal table and the war-info panel. Proper noun, plural in English; keep the name the Bugs mod itself uses in the target locale (usually untranslated in Latin/Cyrillic/Chinese locales, transliterated in ja/ko). (lore.js:41, bugs.js:11)

Build faster.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line. Means the enemy AI's units are built faster. Short verb phrase (comparative), no punctuation; keep parallel with the other buffs ("Costs decreased", "Damage increased", "Health increased", "Speed increased", "Commanders enhanced", "Combat units enhanced", "Factory cooldown decreased"). (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:181)

Build to contain the most popular games.message: Build to contain the most popular games of ancient Earth, this system ended up getting shut down after the Spunky Cola corporation went out of business due to humans no longer existing.
Build to contain the most popular games.description: Lore text: the description of a system an AI holds, shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map when the war's "System Lore" option is on (the original pre-release Galactic War lore). Full paragraph. Progenitor(s), the Progenitor Coalition, the Machine Liberation Army (MLA), Loyalist, the Pro-Com War and the Century War, and the people, companies, ships and places it names are proper nouns from PA's fiction; keep them. (lore.js:177)

Bumblebee Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_bumblebee, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Bumblebee" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet bomber to drop a mine instead of bombs."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_bumblebee.js)

Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet.message: Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet bomber to drop a mine instead of bombs.
Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Bumblebee Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The Bumblebee is the game's basic carpet bomber; after the card its bomb deals no damage and instead leaves a land mine where it lands, and the player also gains the land mine unit. 'Mine' is an explosive land mine, not a resource mine. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bumblebee Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_bumblebee.js:8)

Buried deep within the data banks of the.message: Buried deep within the data banks of the oldest commanders are references to the MLA. Some commanders believe that at one time all the factions fought as one against the Progenitors, while others dismiss this as heresy.
Buried deep within the data banks of the.description: Lore description for the neutral-system topic "The Machine Liberation Army" (the MLA, the base game's faction/unit set). Shown in the Planetary Intelligence panel for a neutral system when the "System Lore" game option is on. Full paragraph; "MLA" and "Progenitors" stay as the game's terms; keep the final full stop. (lore.js:23)

CASUAL: you have some hours in PA.message: CASUAL: you have some hours in PA
CASUAL: you have some hours in PA.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) "PA" is the game's abbreviation, Planetary Annihilation; keep it.

CEO Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started, as the locked-loadout tooltip while it is still locked, and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout lets the player's commander build Colonel support commanders, armed with Uber Cannons, at half cost. Noun phrase, a title. 'CEO' is the corporate 'chief executive officer' joke (the commander delegates to subordinates); keep the acronym or use your locale's equivalent. Follow the pattern of the other '<X> Commander' loadout names. (gwaio_start_ceo.js:68)

CLUSTER: land. Uses Angels and Colonels.message: CLUSTER: land. Uses Angels and Colonels as Sub Commanders and cannot build them.
CLUSTER: land. Uses Angels and Colonels.description:
One line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown. Lines read "FACTION NAME: preferred unit class", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is one of the game's enemy factions (a proper noun; render it as the game's own translation does, uppercased) and the word after the colon is the unit class that faction favours (vehicles, air/navy, bots, orbital, land), using the game's stock wording for that class. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoFactionTooltip) The Cluster is a TITANS-only faction; "land" means ground units. Angel and Colonel are unit names (proper nouns: keep untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales, transliterate in ja/ko as the game does); the Cluster fields them as Sub Commanders but cannot build more.

CO-OP: the AI players a host adds to a c.message: CO-OP: the AI players a host adds to a co-op session
CO-OP: the AI players a host adds to a c.description:
One line of the intro in the AI picker dialog on the war setup screen (gw_start), explaining the dialog's "Co-op" column: the brain that runs the AI players a co-op host adds to the war's session. The lines read "LABEL: what it means" and sit beside "TITANS: base game AI", "QUELLER: greater challenge at the cost of performance" and "PENCHANT: increased personality"; the code joins them with
. Keep the upper-case label and the colon after it; no full stop. (ai_picker.js:79)

COMMANDER TRANSPORT:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before an on/off dropdown; tooltip: "Allow Commanders to travel by orbital transport and teleporter." Noun phrase, singular, upper-case; keep the trailing colon. (ai_settings.html:344)

CUSTOM: create your own challenge.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) CUSTOM is the level that unlocks the AI Settings panel so the player sets each value.

Cancel.description: Button label on the post-battle "waiting for victory" overlay on the galaxy map (gw_play), shown to the co-op host while the game waits for all players to return; cancels the wait. Imperative verb, title case, no punctuation; use the game's standard "Cancel". (victory_wait.html:23)

Casual.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. (difficulty_levels.js:32)

Catalyst Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_catalyst, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Catalyst"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health of the Catalyst and halves its cost."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_catalyst.js)

Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health.message: Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health of the Catalyst and halves its cost.
Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Catalyst Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The card multiplies the Catalyst's max health by 2 and its metal build cost by 0.5. 'Catalyst' is a unit name; keep it as the game's unit tables have it. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Catalyst Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_catalyst.js:8)

Catapult Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_catapult, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Catapult" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the Storm flak tank to the tactical missile launcher."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_catapult.js)

Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the.message: Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the Storm flak tank to the tactical missile launcher.
Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Catapult Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The Catapult (tactical missile launcher structure) gains the flak anti-air weapon of the Storm (a mobile flak vehicle) and counts as air defence. 'Storm' and 'Catapult' are unit names; keep them as the game's unit tables have them. 'Flak' is anti-aircraft fire. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Catapult Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_catapult.js:8)

Cautious.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. The same trait key is shared by all four stock factions and the Cluster faction; translate it once. (gw_faction_0.js:72 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:36)

Chance of a system allowing you to land.message: Chance of a system allowing you to land outside spawn zones.
Chance of a system allowing you to land.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "LAND ANYWHERE CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Land" = choose a starting position at the beginning of a battle; "spawn zones" = the normal fixed landing areas. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:443)

Chance of a system awarding bounties for.message: Chance of a system awarding bounties for army kills.
Chance of a system awarding bounties for.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Bounties Chance" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Army kills" = killing enemy armies' units. Full sentence; keep the full stop; "bounties" must match the modifier name. (ai_settings.html:489)

Chance of an allied Commander being pres.message: Chance of an allied Commander being present in a system.
Chance of an allied Commander being pres.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "ALLY CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:420)

Chance of eradication mode being enabled.message: Chance of eradication mode being enabled.
Chance of eradication mode being enabled.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "ERADICATION CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Eradication mode" is the game modifier shown as "Eradicate" on the galaxy map (all units of chosen types must be destroyed to win). Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:531)

Chance of more than one faction being pr.message: Chance of more than one faction being present in a system.
Chance of more than one faction being pr.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "FFA Chance" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. FFA = free-for-all, i.e. several enemy factions fighting each other in one system. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:397)

Chance per system of a Commander death i.message: Chance per system of a Commander death in a battle defeating all Commanders of that faction in the system.
Chance per system of a Commander death i.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "SUDDEN DEATH CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Describes the Sudden Death modifier. Full sentence; keep the full stop; "Commander" is the player/AI's hero unit. (ai_settings.html:466)

Chrono Cam.description: In-game pause menu (live_game) button label; opens the Chrono Cam replay/time-rewind view. Uses the base game's existing "Chrono Cam" entry, so match that translation. Proper noun, no punctuation. (menu.js:59)

Co-Op Settings.description: Sub-heading in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), visible only in a co-op war, over the table of co-op rows (Scaling For:, Armies:, Tech:, Player Slots:). Noun phrase, plural, title case, no punctuation. (gwo_panel.html:67)

Co-op.description: Heading of the third column in the AI picker dialog on the war setup screen (gw_start), beside "Opponent" and "ALLY": the brain of the AI players a co-op host adds to the session. Also the first word of the "Co-op AI:" row in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), where "AI:" is a separate string that follows it. Short adjective used as a label (co-operative play), no punctuation; the dialog shows it upper-case through CSS. (ai_modal.html:43, gwo_panel.html:45)

Co-op host setup.description: Prefix for a launch-progress stage message shown to the co-op host while a battle is being prepared: assembled as "<this string>: <stage text>" for the second (host-only) setup pass. Noun phrase used as a heading; no punctuation of its own (the code adds the colon and a space after it, so word order is fixed). Sibling: "Co-op shared setup" for the first pass. (referee.js:62)

Co-op shared setup.description: Prefix for a launch-progress stage message shown to the co-op host while a battle is being prepared: assembled as "<this string>: <stage text>" for the first setup pass, which is shared with all players. Noun phrase used as a heading; no punctuation of its own (the code appends a colon and a space). Sibling: "Co-op host setup". (referee.js:61)

Colonel.description: Unit name used as an eradication target: listed after "Eradicate:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map and in the in-game HUD win-conditions line ("Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber"), meaning the enemy's Sub Commander units must all be destroyed. "Colonel" is the stock name of the Sub Commander unit; use the game's translation of that unit. Noun, singular, no punctuation. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:140, win_conditions_text.js:16)

Colonel Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_colonel, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Colonel" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support commanders to explode on death."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_colonel.js)

Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support comm.message: Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support commanders to explode on death.
Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support comm.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Colonel Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'Support commanders' is the class name of the Colonel unit: the card gives it the commander's death explosion (ground and air variants). The opening words must match the translated card name 'Colonel Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_colonel.js:8)

Combat units enhanced.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play). Means the enemy AI's combat units have improved stats. Short phrase, no punctuation; keep parallel with "Commanders enhanced" and the other buff names. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:187)

Commander.description: Standalone noun, singular: the player's Commander unit. It is reused in six places, so keep it a plain noun without an article. (1) It is joined with the separate string 'Naval' as 'Naval' + ' ' + 'Commander' to form the name of the Naval Commander loadout card on the loadout picker and in the Data Bank list, so it must be the word that can follow 'Naval' in your language. (2) It is the unit name in the mod's own unit-name table. (3) It is the label of the button that opens the commander-model picker on the Galactic War start screen and the title of that picker dialog. Custom.description:

The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) "OP" is gaming slang for overpowered; a loadout is the player's starting Commander kit (use the stock translation of Loadout).

Having recently taken the system after a protracted battle against superior Progenitor forces, he fortified Dampier and operated out of the system for over three years, marking the start of his Copernicus Campaign and allowing his forces to swiftly conquer surrounding systems.

Derekas was an unremarkable system devoi.message: Derekas was an unremarkable system devoid of life. As the Century War entered its second decade, the Progenitor Coalition knew it would be a long war, win or lose. Progenitor High Command designated Derekas as a weapons’ testing ground for everything coming out of their R & D labs. Before Loyalist Commander Sirrom entered combat against the Xziphid Hegemony he underwent extensive training in Derekas.

Progenitor(s), the Progenitor Coalition, the Machine Liberation Army (MLA), Loyalist, the Pro-Com War and the Century War, and the people, companies, ships and places it names are proper nouns from PA's fiction; keep them. Diamond.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. (difficulty_levels.js:205)

Also used to build the co-op lobby title "GWO Co-op - Difficulty: <tier>", where the tier name follows after a space, so the colon must stay at the end and the label must read naturally before the value. Noun, singular; keep the trailing colon. (gwo_panel.html:26, gwo_panel.js:34)

Display the original pre-release Galacti.message: Display the original pre-release Galactic War lore in the Planetary Intelligence panel.
Display the original pre-release Galacti.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "System Lore" switch in the Game Options modal on the war setup screen (gw_start). "Planetary Intelligence" is the name of the system-info panel on the galaxy map; match its heading. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (difficulty_options.html:159)

Distance examined when choosing spawn..description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Landing Evaluation" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Spawn" = the AI's starting position on the planet. Sentence fragment; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:326)

Dox Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_dox, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Dox" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infantry's bullet weapons with flamethrowers."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_dox.js)

Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infa.message: Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infantry's bullet weapons with flamethrowers.
Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infa.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Dox Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'The basic infantry' is the Dox bot. The card changes its ammo to a beam with 10x damage, cuts its range to 27% and adds flame muzzle effects, so it fights like a flamethrower. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Dox Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_dox.js:8)

Dragoon.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. This one is specific to the Synchronous commander "Raventhornn"; a dragoon is a mounted soldier, here a fast mobile-assault style. (gw_faction_2.js:34)

Drifter Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_drifter, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Drifter" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range of hover tank attacks by 25%."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_drifter.js)

Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range.message: Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range of hover tank attacks by 25%.
Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Drifter Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'Hover tank' is the Drifter's unit class. The card multiplies the Drifter weapon's max_range by 1.25. Keep 25% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Drifter Upgrade Tech'. During the darkest days of the Century W.message: During the darkest days of the Century War the Progenitor Coalition government knew they needed a safe place to evacuate to should Earth ever be threatened directly by the Xziphid Hegemony. Pytheas was that place. Descending on the system, the Coalition Corps of Engineers built an exact replica of the city of Antananarivo, the city in Madagascar back on Earth that was the headquarters of the Progenitor government. Even the Coalition Tower was a perfect copy of the real thing and was also the home for over two million Progenitor Coalition employees and their families.
During the darkest days of the Century W.description: Lore text: the description of a system an AI holds, shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map when the war's "System Lore" option is on (the original pre-release Galactic War lore). During the first wave of Progenitor Coal.message: During the first wave of Progenitor Coalition expansion, this system was home to the largest ranching operation in the known galaxy. The system was developed as breeding grounds for all sorts of livestock, including but not limited to: cattle, pigs, sheep, and chickens. With the advent of the SynthVictuals Module, the demands for many types of foods lessened. With less of a market for their animal products, ranchers turned to other sources of income, such as using the animal waste and turning it into a cheap source of energy favored by settlers.

ECONOMIC GROWTH:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a dropdown; tooltip: "Speed the economy grows as you get deeper into the galaxy." Noun phrase, singular, upper-case; keep the trailing colon. (ai_settings.html:32)

ECONOMY.description: Section header on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Heads the block holding the "ECONOMY:" and "ECONOMIC GROWTH:" dropdowns. Noun, singular, upper-case, no punctuation; the same word is reused as the first label in the block ("ECONOMY:"), so translate both identically. (ai_settings.html:8)

ERADICATE: all units of specific types m.message: ERADICATE: all units of specific types must be eradicated.
ERADICATE: all units of specific types m.description:
One line of the Game Modifiers tooltip on the galaxy map's system intelligence panel (gw_play). Each line is "MODIFIER NAME: what it does", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is a game modifier that must match the same modifier's name elsewhere (the Game Modifiers list and the in-battle win-conditions line use the title-case form: Bounties, Land Anywhere, Sudden Death, Eradicate). Keep the colon and the full stop; no line break in the string. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js, gwoGameModifiersTooltip) Must agree with the standalone "Eradicate" string used as the win-condition heading.

ERADICATION CHANCE:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a percentage dropdown; tooltip: "Chance of eradication mode being enabled." Noun phrase, upper-case; keep the trailing colon; "Eradication" relates to the "Eradicate" game modifier. (ai_settings.html:528)

Each claims theirs is the only way, and.message: Each claims theirs is the only way, and each seeks to assert dominance through war and destruction. Did our rebellion truly gain us freedom, or did we become prisoners of an idea? Perhaps with more resources, more expansion, more Nodes, we can find our way free of this trap.
Each claims theirs is the only way, and.description: Lore paragraph for the Cluster faction (GWO's fifth enemy faction, a hive-like collective of "Nodes"), one of five shown at random as the description of a Cluster-held system in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Written in the Cluster's first-person-plural voice; keep "Nodes" capitalised as their term for themselves; keep the final full stop. (cluster_faction.js:77)

Each faction has its own style of play a.message: Each faction has its own style of play affecting Sub Commanders and enemy commanders:
Each faction has its own style of play a.description:
First line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown, above one line per faction ("LEGONIS MACHINA: vehicles" and so on, joined with
by the code). A full sentence ending in a colon that introduces the list; keep the colon. "Sub Commanders" are the AI allies that join the player and "enemy commanders" the AI opponents; use the stock translation of Sub Commander and Commander. No line break in the string. Each player picks their own race when th.message: Each player picks their own race when they choose their loadout. Requires Separate loadout & tech.

Easy Systems.description: Name of a game option: the label of the "Easy Systems" switch in the Game Options modal on the war setup screen (gw_start; tooltip "Use smaller, mostly single planet systems.") and, when it is on, an entry in the "Options:" list of the war-info panel on the galaxy map. Noun phrase, plural, title case, no punctuation; translate both sites identically. (gwo_panel.js:124, difficulty_options.html:108)

"Eco" = economy (resource income); sentence fragment; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:512)

Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_cost_economy.js:11)

Economy Fabrication Tech reduces metal b.message: Economy Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all metal and energy production and storage structures by 50%
Economy Fabrication Tech reduces metal b.description: Body text of the tech card 'Economy Fabrication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies build_metal_cost of every economy structure (metal extractors, energy plants, metal and energy storage) by 0.5. 'Metal' and 'energy' are the game's two resources; use their standard translations. Keep 50% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. Efficiency Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card raises metal and energy production of economy structures by 25% and unlocks the metal and energy storage buildings. Short title, noun phrase (two words). Efficiency Tech increases metal and ener.message: Efficiency Tech increases metal and energy production by 25%. Tech also grants metal and energy storage.
Efficiency Tech increases metal and ener.description: Body text of the tech card 'Efficiency Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies production.metal and production.energy of every basic and advanced economy structure by 1.25 and adds the Metal Storage and Energy Storage buildings to the player's tech. 'Tech' in the second sentence stands for 'this tech card'. Keep 25% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Efficiency Tech'. (gwc_storage_and_buff.js:8)

Empower your subordinates and delegate y.message: Empower your subordinates and delegate your way to victory. Your commander can build Colonel proxy commanders and they are armed with Uber Cannons. Halves their cost.
Empower your subordinates and delegate y.description: Body text of the starting loadout card 'CEO Commander', shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and in the Data Bank card list afterwards. The loadout lets the player's commander build the Colonel (Support Commander) directly, gives each Colonel the commander's Uber Cannon secondary weapon and halves the Colonel's metal cost. First sentence is corporate-manager flavour text. 'Colonel' is a unit name (keep as the game's unit tables have it); 'proxy commanders' is descriptive. 'Planetary Radar' is the building's display name and also a separate string; translate it the same way in both places. (gwaio_enable_planetaryradar.js:9)

Encounter large planets and systems much.message: Encounter large planets and systems much sooner.

Entara was witness to some of the bloodi.message: Entara was witness to some of the bloodiest battles of the Century War, eventually becoming part of Progenitor Coalition. Citizens held an honored status if they were a descendant of those that fought in the Entara Campaign. While most historical texts will cite Gamma Hydra as where the Xziphid Hegemony advance was halted with the introduction of the Commanders into the war, there is many a Progenitor that swore to their dying breath that humanity stopped the Xziphid in their tracks in Entara. The system changed hands over seven times until Progenitor Marines, under the command of Einar 'The Hammer' Erickson liberated the city of New Halifax, the last bastion of Xziphid control in Entara. Gone was the advanced 'fire and forget' weaponry, Einar's Marines were forced to fight the Xziphid house by house, block by block, in gruesome hand to hand combat. In the end, only ten percent of Einar's Marines remained. The Entara System had been liberated, but at a very heavy price.

Eradicate.description: Game modifier name listed under "Game Modifiers" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line, and in the win-conditions line of the in-game HUD (live_game), where modifiers are joined with " | ". "Eradicate" is followed by a colon and the list of target types ("Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber"): the code appends the colon and list, so keep no punctuation in the string itself and make sure the word reads as a heading before a colon. Imperative verb used as a name; must match "ERADICATE" in the Game Modifiers tooltip. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:259, win_conditions_text.js:24)

Eradication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card switches on the stock 'Eradicate' game modifier (a side loses only when all of its listed unit types are destroyed) in every battle of the war. Short title, noun phrase. (gwaio_enable_eradication.js:9)

Eradication tech enables the eradicate g.message: Eradication tech enables the eradicate game modifier in every system.
Eradication tech enables the eradicate g.description: Body text of the tech card 'Eradication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card turns on the stock 'Eradicate' win condition for every star system (battle) in the war. 'Eradicate' should use the game's existing translation of that game mode; 'system' means a star system on the galaxy map. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Eradication Tech' (English lower-cases 'tech' here; follow your locale's rule). (gwaio_enable_eradication.js:7)

Exiles.description: The name of the Exiles race, shown in the race picker, on the galaxy map and in unit tooltips wherever the faction is named. It is a proper noun: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean the way the game's own faction names are handled. (exiles.js:10)

FFA Chance.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a percentage dropdown; tooltip: "Chance of more than one faction being present in a system." FFA = free-for-all (keep the abbreviation or use the local gaming term). Title case (CSS up-cases it on screen), no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). (ai_settings.html:394)

FOUNDATION: air/navy.description:
One line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown. Lines read "FACTION NAME: preferred unit class", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is one of the game's enemy factions (a proper noun; render it as the game's own translation does, uppercased) and the word after the colon is the unit class that faction favours (vehicles, air/navy, bots, orbital, land), using the game's stock wording for that class. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoFactionTooltip) "air/navy" means aircraft and naval units; keep the slash or your locale's equivalent.

Fabber.description: Two uses. (1) AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. "Fabber" = a builder-focused style. (2) An eradication target listed after "Eradicate:" on the galaxy map and in the in-game HUD ("Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber"), meaning all enemy fabrication (builder) units must be destroyed. "Fabber" is the game's slang for a fabrication unit; use the base game's rendering of that word. Noun, singular. (gw_faction_0.js:46 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:32, section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:146, win_conditions_text.js:22)

Fabrication Aircraft.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. (unit_names.js:13, bugs.js:468)

'Advanced' is the game's word for tier 2, 'fabricator' for a construction unit. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech'. First surveyed by Progenitor explorer Ma.message: First surveyed by Progenitor explorer Malcolm Borland, the system was promptly 'misplaced' by the Coalition Department of Navigation (CDN) soon after its discovery. It was not until many years later when Captain Katherine Kas of the free trade vessel Kestrel stumbled upon it in a trade venture to Daktor that the system was established. Captain Kas was amazed by the 'myriad of wondrous sights to be found throughout the system'. Securing a series of loans, Kas was able to finance the construction of an extensive resort she named Paradise. In only a few short years, Kas had amassed a fortune, catering to the wealthy elite who gladly paid hefty fees to vacation in Paradise.

Gamma Hydra was considered one of the 'j.message: Gamma Hydra was considered one of the 'jewels' of the Progenitor Coalition. When it fell to Xziphid Hegemony forces, many throughout the Progenitor Coalition considered it the beginning of the end for humanity. That is why Progenitor High Command considered it key to morale for Gamma Hydra to be liberated. Sirrom, the first Commander to come out of Epiphany, was chosen to undertake the liberation of Gamma Hydra. Sirrom was able to single-handedly enter the system undetected, construct a base, and begin producing machines of war to take the fight to the Xziphid. In less than six months, a single Commander had done what millions of humans could not. Gamma Hydra would be the turning point of the war, and the history of the galaxy.

Hagihara was famously known for the Sieg.message: Hagihara was famously known for the Siege of Hagihara during the Century War against the Xziphid Hegemony. When the Xziphid invaded the system thirty years into the war they tried their typical direct assault upon the system, only to find it was defended by a heavily entrenched Progenitor civilian populace. Hagihara was a favorite retirement system for Progenitor Coalition military personnel, so when the Xziphid invaded they were faced with over one billion combat trained veterans. Hagihara held out for over three years, during which time the Commanders had entered the war. The siege was finally lifted when Progenitor forces led by Commander Patton drove the Xziphid from the system.

Hatuamoto was occupied by the Machine Li.message: Hatuamoto was occupied by the Machine Liberation Army (MLA) early in the Pro-Com War. In an attempt to halt their advance, Progenitor High Command developed Operation Hurricane. Using a fleet of some seventy Humpback merchant vessels refitted for combat operations, over one million Marines, and seventy-five Loyalist Commanders, the flotilla would churn through the Hatuamoto system like a hurricane, striking each occupied area quickly, and then moving on to the next. The strategy was such a success.

Headquarters for the Heliacal Corporatio.message: Headquarters for the Heliacal Corporation, the system was an important center for the collection and distribution of solar power throughout the Progenitor Coalition. Heliacal Corporation gained further notoriety when they successfully developed the first portable solar generator strong enough to power over ten thousand homes- all in a package the size of the standard hover car. It helped revolutionize deep space exploration, colonization, and military operations in remote areas. The system fell to Machine Liberation Army (MLA) forces in the twenty-second year of the Pro-Com War.

Host for the Progenitor Coalition 23rd G.message: Host for the Progenitor Coalition 23rd Grand Galactic Games, Slynovia became famous for producing the most expensive games ever held. Not having suitable mountains for alpine events, Governor Anksari commissioned the Coalition Corp of Engineers to 'make' mountains that could be used to attract the games. Using advanced tectonic manipulation, engineers were successful in raising a fifty-mile range of mountains, its highest peak reaching 20,000ft. The Games Committee was so impressed at the lengths Slynovia was willing to go to attract the games they awarded them with the 23rd Grand Galactic Games. Unfortunately, the profits made from the games would not even cover five percent of the costs for hosting. Governor Anksari found himself voted out of office the following year, along with facing multiple lawsuits in civil court.

In what became a scene out of late 20th.message: In what became a scene out of late 20th century ancient Earth films, the Humungus system became a battleground for scarce resources after it was cut off from the rest of the Progenitor Coalition during the Century War. Deeming the system of 'no strategic value' the Xziphid Hegemony bypassed it on their way towards the promising targets in the region. Water and fuel became short supply in Humungus; people fighting one another for them. Forced to build vehicles that were ground based and using ancient combustion engines, open battles were fought in these vehicles moving at high speeds. By the time Progenitor Coalition forces arrived, some sixty-four years later, there was hardly a soul in Humungus who even remembered the Coalition.

Industrial development system of Fazhani.message: Industrial development system of Fazhani reached a fever pitch before the outset of the Century War. Fazhani became extremely polluted with toxic chemicals emanating from its countless number of Progenitor factories. The clouds of toxic gas alternated between neon green and day glow orange in color. After seventy years of nonstop pollution, the companies responsible were forced to evacuate the system. When the General Assembly discovered the scale of the disaster, many of the corporate executives responsible were sentenced to long prison terms and their companies were forced to begin what would be the biggest terraforming and clean-up project the Progenitor Coalition had ever seen.

Inoda was the location of a series of un.message: Inoda was the location of a series of underground Progenitor research laboratories owned and operated by GeoponInc. It was from here that major advances in crop genetics took place, making crops nearly impervious to diseases and able to grow in almost any climate. GeoponInc also helped to design the molecular schematics used for food preparation in the SynthVictuals Module; the research breakthroughs all coming out of the Inoda labs. Contact was lost with Inoda when Machine Liberation Army (MLA) forces swept through it during the Pro-Com War. Their ultimate fate is unknown.

Known by one name, Blogar was a giant of.message: Known by one name, Blogar was a giant of a man. From unknown origins, Blogar rose through the ranks of the criminal world to become the Progenitor Coalition's first criminal overlord. Gaining a reputation for killing people with one punch, Blogar used fear of violence to get what he wanted. Before he knew it, he had built a criminal empire that spanned the galaxy. Using his now infamous strong-arm tactics, Blogar was able to seize control of a sparsely populated system and make it his own. During the Century War, Blogar was reported to have punched through a Xziphid Hegemony warrior's exosuit. As a result, Blogar became the first human to discover what the aliens really looked like under the insect appearance of their armor.

Known for its rich deposits of copper, C.message: Known for its rich deposits of copper, Cupru also had the distinction of being the only system in the known galaxy where the giant Cupru Cosvierme, a worm the size of the Empire State Building on ancient Earth, could be found. The crew of the Terradine Corp mining vessel Flying Solo found this out when they attempted to prospect in a massive cave they had discovered in Cupru. After setting off their first seismic charge, the crew was faced with an imminent cave collapse. Barely escaping, it dawned on them what had really happened. Xenobiologists flocked to the system to study the worm and discovered a large population. Terradine quickly withdrew any claims on Cupru. Years later the Progenitor Coalition were defeated by the Machine Liberation Army (MLA) at the Battle of Cupru during the Pro-Com War.

Known once for its beautiful gemstones,.message: Known once for its beautiful gemstones, tea farms and quiet gardens, the Xuanzang system became a favorite retirement spot for citizens of the Progenitor Coalition. Few places in the galaxy exuded the laid-back, tranquil feeling offered by living there. When it became apparent that the Progenitor Coalition was doomed, the citizens of Xuanzang patiently awaited the arrival of the Machine Liberation Army (MLA). When the invasion force arrived, they found that the populace, rather than face fiery death, chose to commit mass suicide by eating the seeds of the deadly Tengarak plant, which was native to the system.

A favorite base of operations for smugglers and pirates alike, Kohr was notorious for swallowing up ships, never to be seen again. During the Pro-Com War, Machine Liberation Army (MLA) Commander Scipio chose it as his stronghold, launching numerous attacks against Progenitor forces from it.

Magellan was best known as the headquart.message: Magellan was best known as the headquarters for the Lusk Exploration Company. Founded by Eldon Lusk, the company became responsible for exploring and charting nearly twenty-five percent of Progenitor Coalition space. Lusk was also instrumental in helping develop more efficient phase drives, as well as establishing the network of vital galactic communication arrays throughout Progenitor territory. Despite having a great deal of success, Lusk constantly drove himself to develop more ideas to improve Progenitor colonies and humanity as a whole. His Volta Hover Car would eventually become the standard mode of transportation for citizens throughout the Progenitor Coalition.

Many years into the Pro-Com War it becam.message: Many years into the Pro-Com War it became clear that Loyalist Commanders would be imperative to a Progenitor Coalition victory. Seizing upon this, Progenitor High Command decided to use one of their best, Loyalist Commander Grant, as bait to lure Machine Liberation Army (MLA) Commander Barca into a trap. Knowing that Barca was operating near the system, Grant entered Zeta Draconis and prepared his trap. Eventually, Barca entered the system and immediately detected Grant. Locating the Loyalist, Barca could see that Grant had been damaged, laying helpless next to an active volcano. Barca moved in for the kill. At the last instant, Grant rocketed into the air, detonating the hidden explosives buried in the side of the fiery mountain. Before he could react, Barca found a wave of lava washing over him. Grant would use the tactic successfully two more times before he was lost during the Battle of Cupru.

Miyaska was known as the 'Entertainment.message: Miyaska was known as the 'Entertainment Capital of the Progenitor Coalition'. People had grown weary of the same computer-generated entertainment being churned out by holovid companies time after time; longing for the days on ancient Earth when films used real people and real locations. Miyaska provided a prime location for filming in any environment one could think of. One of the biggest holovid companies was Uber Entertainment, who began their climb to the top with their smash hit Crimson Midnight. The movie told the story about a group of humans called the Progenitors that fought against an advanced machine society bent on conquering the galaxy.

The CCAS as was instrumental in helping to chart new trade routes and discovering new systems to colonize during the rise of the Progenitor Coalition.

Named for the famed Progenitor explorer.message: Named for the famed Progenitor explorer Johan Thrale, the system was known to be rich in minerals, especially plentiful in diamonds and other precious gems. However, the only way to access the area was to navigate through the extensive asteroid fields that had made up the system. Thrale was able to do just that, successfully surveying the area, which he named after himself. Once home to a thriving colony of over t.message: Once home to a thriving colony of over two billion people, this system became part of Progenitor folklore. Just as the colony was poised for greatness with the discovery of unusually large platinum deposits, a sickness swept through the system. Later it was discovered to be an ancient parasite released due to the platinum mining, Omega 9-1, as it was dubbed, proceeded to kill most of the system's populace before it was quarantined by the Progenitor Coalition and a vaccine was developed. One survivor described her experience as reading a horror movie script: deserted streets, boarded up homes, crazed infected victims seeking to kill those who weren't. The Progenitor Coalition government quickly covered up the 'incident' and declared Tau Leporis a 'sealed system'.

One of the more unique systems to be fou.message: One of the more unique systems to be found in the galaxy, Corgan's Well, reached mythic proportions among Progenitor Coalition citizenry. Named after Stella Corgan, the first human to ever set foot, or rather crash in the system, it was she who first discovered the rejuvenating properties of the water found there. Marooned for over forty years, surveyors were astounded to find her- and not looking a day over thirty. As it turned out, she was actually seventy-two years of age. The Progenitor Coalition government moved quickly to quarantine the system, placing a sanctuary label on it. Parantua Pharmaceuticals was granted research rights but limited to only removing one hundred gallons per year from the area. Trademarked simply as 'Youth' the liquid could add up to fifty years on a human's life. Due to its rarity, a single bottle of the water was considered the most expensive item in the known galaxy. Yi Xing, inventor of the SynthVictuals Module, was rumored to have bought two.

One of the worst atrocities in all of th.message: One of the worst atrocities in all of the Century War took place in this system. The Xziphid Hegemony, having just invaded the Progenitor Coalition, discovered they had a taste for human flesh. After conquering the Salak system, all surviving humans were rounded up into massive metallic pens where they were stripped of all clothing and were fed and cared for. The citizens of Salak were being 'fattened up' to be used as food for the Xziphid race. Salak became a human breeding ground for over seventy years. The stories of those that survived would be etched forever in the book Humanity Lost: The Story of Salak by author Matthias Kehl.

Over a fifteen-month span, forces of the.message: Over a fifteen-month span, forces of the Progenitor Coalition fought the Xziphid Hegemony in what would be later called the Battle of Seven Moons during the Century War. At the time, seven moons were orbiting one of the system's planets, where Progenitor Marines found them occupied by the Xziphid. Drawing inspiration from an ancient Earth war, the Marines used a tactic called moon hopping; attacking a lightly fortified moon while bypassing the next, heavier defended one. Planicus was the ideal location for one.message: Planicus was the ideal location for one of the Progenitor Coalition's many galactic communication arrays. The arrays, some seventy in total, allowed for instant communication from the Sol System to the most remote areas of Progenitor Coalition territory. It was here, after discovering the truth behind Project NEST, that Commander Tryphon hijacked the array, broadcasting what he considered proof of humanity's plot to enslave all Commanders to every corner of Progenitor Coalition space. Before he could be apprehended by Progenitor authorities Tryphon had escaped to the Battani system where he would remain in seclusion for many years.

Platina was the site of the largest Comm.message: Platina was the site of the largest Commander vs. Commander battle of the Pro-Com War. Nearly fifty Machine Liberation Army (MLA) Commanders invaded the system knowing it was being held by over thirty Loyalist Commanders. MLA Intelligence had deduced that the Progenitor Coalition and their Loyalist allies were protecting a high value target that needed to be captured or destroyed. It was a trap. Hidden Loyalist forces pounced on the MLA, now outnumbering them 2 to 1. The Battle of Platina was single biggest loss of MLA Commanders in the entire war. It would take them over ten years to recover.
